title: Electron Microscopy of Ag Nanoparticles on ZrO2-TiO2 Heterojunction to Improve the Photocatalytic Arsenic Oxidation
content: In this research, Ag is loaded on the ZrO2-TiO2 heterojunction to improve the photocatalytic Arsenic oxidation. Arsenic removal is considered a challenge and an environmental priority [1]. In this sense, different semiconducting materials have been studied; among them, TiO2 has been investigated due to its low cost, non-toxicity and physicochemical properties [2]; however, this semiconductor has a rapid recombination of electron-hole pairs under illumination. TiO2 has been coupled with other semiconductors (e.g. ZrO2) to increase the charge carriers' lifetime. Zhou et al. studied a TiO2- ZrO2 material under UV and visible light irradiation, concluding that arsenic oxidation occurs through the photogenerated holes [3]. At the same time, TiO2 can be decorated with metallic nanoparticles and/or metallic oxides (e.g. Ag NP, AgO, Ag2O) to enhance the photocatalytic activity. In this investigation, ZrO2-TiO2 heterojunction (ZT) was synthesized by sol-gel method. A mixture of zirconium butoxide, titanium butoxide, nitric acid and butanol was stirred, then the hydrolysis was performed and the material was dried and calcined at 400°C. Subsequently, 0.5 wt. of Ag was deposited on the ZT heterojunction through precipitation [4]. The ZT heterojunction was suspended in a solution with AgNO3, and then, NaOH was added to reach a pH of 9.0. The suspension was washed and dried at 150 °C for 2 hours.
